classification: descriptive allocator lifecycle and explicit caller-drop observations
inputs: Reuse the exact existing plain/media-rich PPTX lifecycle corpus builders and their semantic/preservation/refusal gates. Owned and source-backed source/destination hashes must match for each corpus.
observation: Allocator-only explicit retention subcommand; absolute callback counters at input preparation, open, plan, publication and explicit ordered drops, plus one whole-cycle region peak. The input clones and output reservation are included in this new cycle. Existing timing selector boundaries are unchanged.
capture_constraints: Fixed preallocated scalar observation storage; no reporting, hashing, reopen or process-stat allocations between endpoint checkpoints.
Exact output byte comparison against independently prevalidated corpus output before sink drop on every iteration.
Allocation counters must be available, nonoverflowed and observer-valid. Retain cumulative counters and derive checked stage differences.
Record live ownership sets per checkpoint, including publication result, plan, document handles, caller source Arcs and sink. Owned input Vecs move into packages.
Fresh process for each role/repeat. Root serializes all task Cargo/build/test/profiling and capture workloads; shared-host activity is uncontrolled.
Freeze harness/protocol in a commit before release build and formal capture. Bind revision, source manifest, binary, protocol, report, corpus and output hashes.
Keep raw rows in capture order; summarize every boundary, signed change from entry, after-drop residual and repeat drift. No geometric-mean aggregation across APIs.
Review nonzero post-drop residual or repeat drift above 5% in nonzero phase changes; do not relabel retained observations as object-owned bytes or leaks.
Portable replay and adversarial report mutations must pass after copied executable and task-temporary cleanup. Retain failures and lossless log custody.
scope_limits: No optimization, latency, throughput, physical-copy, cache-occupancy, managed-budget or RSS-release claim.
Absolute callback live bytes are process-global and can include unrelated threads; they are not object-owned or allocator-internal memory.
The source-backed source observer and output reservation are declared owners in these observations.
Whole-process resource usage may be retained separately as context, but is not a phase-specific RSS observation.
Near-limit/pinning/eviction/repeated-publication, native/cold/range, broad CRUD, streaming and scaling gates remain open.
